newsitem.title: UK: GKN H1 stg sting seen worse than predicted.
newsitem.headline: GKN H1 stg sting seen worse than predicted.

text.p: UK engineering giant GKN Plc is expected to receive a bigger sting from sterling than it has previously estimated when its reports half-year results next Wednesday.

In May, GKN chairman David Lees told the annual shareholder meeting that the translational effect of the pound's surge would wipe 10 million stg off profits. But he said despite this profits remained ahead of the same period last year.
But since that statement was made the pound has continued to advance against the mark and is now around the three mark level.

Analysts are thus expecting a harder currency hit, but still expect profits to remain ahead of last year. Interim profits are forecast to be between 185 million and 193 million, versus a post-exceptional 181 million in 1996.
The interim dividend is pitched at between 10.0 pence and 10.5 pence per share, versus 9.6 pence before.
"The TI Group figures yesterday (Thursday) showed that most people had not gone far enough to compensate for the currency issue," said one engineering analyst.
Like TI, GKN is more exposed to the currency translational impact of stg than the transactional effect, because it has a lot of overseas production.
This underestimate by analysts meant a probable downward revision of expectations for GKN as well, he said.
GKN has notable exposure to stg's moves against the market. Out of total annual sales of around three billion pounds, around 1.1 billion is to continental Europe.
Looking at expectations for divisional results, one analyst said he expected a "soggy" performance from the automotive parts unit due to competitive conditions in Europe, especially France.
But Zafar Khan, analyst at SocGen, said he expected a "reasonable" underlying performance, before accounting for stg's translational impact on profits.
On the GKN Westland side, there is a concern among some analysts that planned deliveries of helicopters next year may slip back to 1999, delaying the ensuing profit uplift.
The key positive factor expected within the results is the Chep pallet unit which is seen performing well.
Cash flow is also seen remaining strong.
